text.p: Perpetual Trustees Australia Ltd said on Monday it planned to make potentially substantial acquisitions this financial year, most likely in Australia but possibly in the region as well.
Managing director Graham Bradley told Reuters that the company, the largest trustee operation in Australia, was targetting the asset administration sector.
Bradley would not say how much could be spent but noted that Perpetual Trustees had no debt, a strong borrowing capacity, and could liquidate A$60 million in equities to help fund any takeover.

Expanding on the 1995/96 annual report which identified strategic acquisitions as part of this year's growth strategy, Bradley said other firms were preparing to leave targetted areas such as superannuation master trusts and private superannuation because of regulatory complexity and high costs.

"We very much believe we can grow in the provision of back office investment accounting and other services to fund managers," he added. "At the moment there is virtually no one providing outsourced investment accounting for fund managers in thic country whereas in the United States 80 percent of fund managers use one of three outsource suppliers."
Bradley said Perpetual Trustees had not reduced its list of possible takeover targets to what he would call a "hit list".
The takeover strategy focussed on Australia, but international expansion was a possibility in 1996/97.
"We are beginning a reconnaissance of opportunities in Singapore, Malaysia and New Zealand," he said.

"But at this stage none of them look as attractive as domestic opportunities." The annual report forecast continued higher net profit in 1996/97, but not as large as the 29.4 percent increase achieved last year which which took net profit to a record A$14.56 million. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
